## Before you begin

Before you set up Database Observability, ensure you have:

- A running PostgreSQL 14.0 or later instance.
- Administrative access to your PostgreSQL server to create a monitoring user, enable extensions, change settings, and restart PostgreSQL if needed.
- Database Observability activated in your Grafana Cloud stack.
- A machine where you can install Grafana Alloy 1.17.0 or later with network access to both your PostgreSQL database and Grafana Cloud.
- Basic familiarity with PostgreSQL database administration.

needsText: Before starting the setup, verify that your environment meets the requirements for Database Observability. Getting these right upfront prevents troubleshooting later.

## Grafana Cloud requirements

| Requirement | Details |
|---|---|
| Account | Grafana Cloud account with Editor or Admin role |
| Database Observability | Activated in your Grafana Cloud stack. Open **Observability** > **Database** in the navigation menu and click **Activate Database Observability** if the app isn't already active. |
| Stack | Access to Grafana Cloud Mimir (metrics) and Grafana Cloud Loki (logs) data sources |
| Permissions | Ability to view and create dashboards |

## PostgreSQL requirements

| Requirement | Details |
|---|---|
| Version | PostgreSQL 14.0 or later |
| pg_stat_statements | Extension loaded through `shared_preload_libraries` and created in each database you monitor |
| Query tracking settings | `compute_query_id` set to `on`, `pg_stat_statements.track` set to `all`, and `track_activity_query_size` set to `4096`. `track_activity_query_size` (like `shared_preload_libraries`) needs a PostgreSQL restart; the others apply on a config reload. |
| Connection | Alloy must connect directly to the database host — avoid load balancers or connection poolers like PgBouncer |
| Monitoring user | User with the `pg_monitor` and `pg_read_all_stats` roles, plus read access to the schemas you want to monitor |

## Grafana Alloy requirements

| Requirement | Details |
|---|---|
| Version | Grafana Alloy 1.17.0 or later. Database Observability is generally available, so no `--stability.level` flag is required. |
| Network | Outbound access to Grafana Cloud endpoints |
| Database access | Network connectivity to your PostgreSQL instance |

Before you begin, install Grafana Alloy 1.17.0 or later on a host that can reach both your PostgreSQL server and Grafana Cloud. Refer to [Install Grafana Alloy](https://grafana.com/docs/alloy/latest/set-up/install/) for your platform. Database Observability is generally available, so you don't need a `--stability.level` flag. Alloy should connect directly to the database host, not through a load balancer or PgBouncer.

The wizard offers two deployment methods. This path uses **Manual configuration**, which works with any Alloy you run yourself. If your collector is enrolled in Fleet Management, you can choose **Fleet Management** instead and Grafana Cloud pushes the configuration to it for you.
